Instant application has been preferred by the applicant(s) namely Ram Prasad S/o Late Ram Dularey, Ravi Kumar S/o Ram Prasad, Santosh S/o Prem Narayan, Suresh S/o Nanhoo, Pankaj S/o Nanhoo, Jai Ram S/o Sankata for quashing the entire proceedings of Complaint Case no. 1545 of 2016 (Anurag Kureel Vs. Ram Prasad and Others) pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Unnao.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is stated that on account of matrimonial dispute between the opposite party no. 2/Anurag Kureel and Meenu Kumari (wife of the opposite party no. 2 and daughter of the applicant no.1/Ram Prasad), an FIR was lodged i.e. Case Crime No. 0433 on 21.07.2015 by Meenu Kumari/wife of the Ram Prasad And Ors. vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Deptt. ... on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162026524/
1 opposite party no. 2 making allegations therein to attract offense under Sections 498A, 323, 504,
506 IPC and Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act against opposite party no. 2/Anurag Kureel (husband), Ramvati (mother-in-law) and Virag (brother in law) and in retaliation, opposite party no. 2/Anurag Kureel filed an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. which was treated as complaint case registered as Complaint Case no. 1545 of 2016 (Anurag Kureel Vs. Ram Prasad and Others) and in the said case, vide order dated 19.04.2016 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Unnao, the applicants were summoned and during the pendency of the case arising out of Case Crime No. 0433, indicated above, the dispute between the opposite party no. 2/Anurag Kureel. and Meenu Kumari was settled and now both the persons are living happily as husband and wife under one roof and in this view of the matter, the parties have entered into a compromise and a copy of compromise deed, duly signed by the parties, is annexed as Annexure No. SA-1 to the supplementary affidavit (IA No. 12 ot 2024).

entities.text: Anurag Kureel Vs. Ram Prasad and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, keeping in view the settlement arrived at between the parties and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in this regard, the proceedings impugned are liable to be quashed.

Whether the parties have, in fact, compromised the matter or not, can best be ascertained by the Trial Court as such compromise has to be duly verified in presence of the parties concerned before the Court.

Considering the aforesaid, this application is disposed of finally in following terms:-
(i) The parties to the proceedings in issue shall appear and file the compromise before the concerned Court within four week's from today.
(ii) If the parties appear before the concerned Court in terms of above, the concerned Court shall proceed to verify the compromise between the parties to the proceedings and prepare a report to the same effect and the original compromise deed be made part of record.
(iii) The concerned Court shall conclude the process of verification of compromise within two week's from the date of production of copy of this order.
(iv) The concerned Court shall permit the parties to the proceedings to obtain the certified copy of the report as well as compromise deed.
(v) It shall be open to the applicant(s) to approach this Court again for quashing of the proceedings.
(vi) Office is directed to provide original compromise to the counsel for the applicant(s), after retaining its photocopy on record.
It is for the purposes for its verification by the concerned Court.
(vii) For a period of eight weeks, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant(s) in the aforesaid case.
